_comment_slot: Its own replication slot and publication. The ledger connector has its own, and two connectors sharing a slot would each see only part of the stream — whichever read a change first would consume it.
plugin.name: pgoutput
slot.name: payments_outbox
publication.name: payments_outbox_pub
_comment_snapshot: The outbox is a queue, not history. On first start there is nothing worth replaying, and a snapshot of rows that may already have been published would duplicate them.
_comment_router: The outbox event router unwraps the envelope: the Kafka key becomes aggregate_id (the transfer id) so one transfer's events share a partition and stay ordered, and the message value becomes the payload column rather than a Debezium change record. A consumer that saw TransferCompensated before TransferCompleted would have to reason about a payment that was reversed before it succeeded.
_comment_timestamp: created_at is deliberately NOT mapped as the event timestamp. The router requires an INT64 epoch and a TIMESTAMPTZ arrives as a string, so mapping it fails the task with 'Field created_at is not of type INT64'. Debezium's own source timestamp is used instead, and the business time is requestedAt inside the payload anyway.
_comment_deletes: Pruning deletes published rows. Those deletes must not be published as events, or every consumer sees a tombstone for a transfer that genuinely finished. skipped.operations drops them at the connector so the router never sees one; table.op.invalid.behavior is only the fallback if one somehow reaches it, and it accepts warn|error|fatal rather than skip.
